summary: John's 6th-great-grandmother; wife of Ensign Thomas Lamoreaux and the bridge from the Pennsylvania lines to the Long Island colonial Tuthill/Smith ancestry.
bio:
Keturah Tuttle was born in Dec 1755 at Woodbury Clove, Orange Co., NY (SAR application ACN 58344 gives 1755 at 'Woodbury Clove', matching Alva Tuttle). She was probably a daughter of John Tuthill (c.1730-c.1770) and Temperance Smith (Alva Tuttle, Tuttle-Tuthill Lines, 1968, p.311: children twins James & John 1753, twins Ezekiel & William c.1754, Keturah ~1755, Samuel and Daniel); her children's names James, Temperance and Keturah follow that family. Her uncles Capt. Francis Smith and Capt. Austin Smith commanded the Woodbury Clove and Upper Clove militia companies in 1775-76, with her husband as ensign. She married Thomas Lamoreaux and moved with him to Plymouth (1790) and Jackson Twp. His will left her 'my best horse saddle & bridle' and $100. She died 10 Mar 1833 (obituary, Republican Farmer, Wilkes-Barre, 13 Mar 1833; WikiTree Tuthill-530; Find a Grave 269816651, Lamoreaux Family Burying Ground, Jackson Twp). The tree's death of 1842 (tree shows 1755-1842) is her daughter Keturah's (Harvey Book p.360). (Her Tuttle/Smith ancestors are covered in the colonial section.)

No record found this round names Keturah's parents directly, so her parentage stays probable. New circumstantial support: the 1775 Cornwall Precinct association list carries both 'James Tuttle' and 'John Tuthill' as well as her husband Thomas Lamoureux ([R4-S3]). On Alva Tuttle's reconstruction these are her twin brothers James and John (b. 1753). Her mother Temperance Smith's place in the family of James Smith & Jerusha Topping is now backed by two independent printed authorities: Pelletreau (1898) and C. H. Weygant's Family Record (1897), which names James and Jerusha's daughters Eunice, Keturah, Temperance and Jerusha and puts Capt. Austin and Capt. Francis Smith, their sons, at Woodbury Clove 'some twenty years or more' before the Revolution ([R4-S1], [R4-S2]). Keturah was evidently named for her aunt Keturah Smith.

The printed list of pre-1784 New York marriage licenses has no Lamoreaux-Tuthill (or Tuthill-Smith) entry, so these marriages were probably by banns ([R4-S4]).
sources: Alva M. Tuttle, Tuttle-Tuthill Lines in America (1968) p.311 (FamilySearch Books item 481721: https://www.familysearch.org/library/books/records/item/481721)

researchLog.note: Imported from the project handoff (research rounds 1–3, Oct 2026).
Death in the Ancestry tree: 09 Dec 1842; research: 1833-03-10.

Round 4 relationship evidence (parent I282608055634, probable): Temperance appears among the daughters of James Smith & Jerusha Topping in two independent compiled sources (Pelletreau 1898; Weygant 1897). Keturah's own children bear the names Temperance and Keturah, and her husband served under Temperance's brother Capt. Francis Smith.

Round 4 searched without result: NY marriage licenses before 1784 (1860 printed list, full text): no Tuthill/Tuttle-Smith license; no Lamoreaux-Tuthill license; Abstracts of Wills, NY Surrogate (NYHS Collections), all volumes 1730-1784 on archive.org, full text: no will or administration for John Tuthill of Cornwall/Woodbury Clove, James Tuthill (d. c.1772) or Temperance Tuthill; no will of James Smith of Moriches; Find a Grave 269816651: not re-fetched (site blocked in earlier rounds)

Round 4: added Weygant 1897 as a second independent source for the Smith-Topping family and found 1775 Cornwall association signers James Tuttle and John Tuthill; marriage licenses and NY will abstracts negative.
